newsitem.title: UK: Diana juggles men, mines under media spotlight.
newsitem.headline: Diana juggles men, mines under media spotlight.

text.p: From men to minefields, Princess Diana juggled fresh controversy on Thursday with reports of a glamorous new love in her life just as she heads to Bosnia to crusade against landmines.
The Mirror newspaper declared that the divorced princess had "found love again" after a luxury cruise with a jet-setter called Dodi, heir to the Harrods department store fortune.
Dodi -- a man with a taste for gorgeous women -- is the son of Egyptian tycoon Mohamed Al Fayed and nephew of eminent Saudi entrepreneur Adnan Khashoggi.
Dodi has known Diana for a decade but the pair has never been linked before this week's trip on a yacht called Jonikal that papers dubbed the Love Boat.

"Dodi was hoping to keep this quiet and to be honest he thought he had got away with it," the Mirror quoted a source close to him as saying. "It's too early to tell they are in love, but certainly there is a very close relationship developing and he is very fond of her."
The tabloids said a bidding war was already under way in Paris for "intimate" shots of Dodi and Di at sea.
Newspapers have closely monitored the men in Diana's life since her marriage to Prince Charles ended in 1996.
Only last month Diana, 36, was criticised for holidaying in St Tropez with the Al Fayed family and her two sons, who are next in line for the throne after their father.
That trip apparently paved the way for her secret Mediterranean break with Dodi -- this time without her children, who were back in Britain with Charles.
"We have had a wonderful holiday," the Sun quoted 41-year-old Dodi as saying.
While Charles was never Diana's sort, the tabloids crowned smooth-talking Dodi her "Mr Perfect".
A polo-playing graduate of Sandhurst military school, he has none of the stuffiness of an English aristocrat.
On the contrary, the Oscar-winning filmmaker is based in Los Angeles, owns homes worldwide and has dated stars from Brooke Shields to Koo Stark to Britt Ekland.

He was briefly married to a model in 1986 and has said once was enough. William Hill bookmakers said on Thursday they had cut the odds on Diana remarrying due to the "increased speculation about her private life".
The focus on love came one day before Diana looked likely to steal humanitarian headlines by flying into Bosnia and highlighting the dangers of landmines.
She has long hoped to be taken seriously as a roving ambassador-cum-"Queen of Hearts" and stirred controversy in January by visiting Angola on another landmines trip.
After frequent clashes with the previous Conservative administration over her involvement in politics, Labour Foreign Secretary Robin Cook gave Diana his blessing.
"If her visit to Bosnia is as successful as her trip to Angola, she will deserve thanks, not brickbats," he said.
Travelling as a guest of the U.S. Landmine Survivors Network, Diana will fly to Sarajevo, visit landmine victims and meet local disability groups and rehabilitation specialists.
She will be met in Sarajevo by the group's founder Ken Rutherford, who lost both legs in Somalia in 1993.
